messages:
sam: Heads-up: we just saw a p99 latency spike (~3.2x) on short-sequence text-gen for hosted region eu-west-1 after last night's infra deploy. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/s/realtime?view=shortseq_p99
anya: saw it too. Is this the driver bump + triton upgrade that went out at 02:30? Deploy-bot: deploy successful: infra/driver v470 -> v481, triton runtime image: triton:2.18.1 -> 2.19.0 at 2026-03-17T02:34:11Z :white_check_mark:
li: quick summary from profiler on a sample request (seq_len=16, batch=8):
```
[profile] kernel chosen: fallback_gemm_v2 (time 1.8ms)
[profile] expected: flash_attn_fwd (time 0.45ms)
[profile] reason: heuristic_mismatch (attention_strategy='auto', fallback_threshold=0.02)
[profile] kv_cache_hits: 0.92, cache_evictions/sec: 18
```
li: profiling shows our autoselect now prefers fallback_gemm for short sequences on this model (opt-level changed somehow). That matches p99 trend (short seqs up, long seqs OK).
derek: interesting — we ship a small autotune table in the runtime. If triton changed kernel launch occupancy calculations the heuristic can flip. Can you paste the kernel_decisions log?
li: grabbing kernel_decisions log grep: `grep "kernel_decision" /var/log/redwood/runtime/kernel_decisions.log | tail -n 8`
```
[2026-03-17T02:34:12Z] model:rwbert@v3 kernel_decision:flash_attn_fwd score=0.98
[2026-03-17T02:34:12Z] model:rwbert@v3 kernel_decision:fallback_gemm_v2 score=1.05  # chosen
[2026-03-17T02:34:12Z] reason: estimated_threads=64 -> estimated_time_ms=1.6
[2026-03-17T02:34:13Z] model:rwbert@v3 kernel_decision:fallback_gemm_v2 score=1.12  # chosen
[2026-03-17T02:34:13Z] kv_prefetch:enabled kv_cache_size=12GB
```
anya: score >1 means fallback was predicted faster by our cost model. We need to find why the cost model changed. Two possibilities: kernel latency model inputs (occupancy, sm_est) or a measured cold-start sample pushed the running avg.
sam: any sign of noisy neighbor / memory pressure on those hosts? The kv cache evictions look suspicious (18/sec).
li: checked host metrics: GPU memory free dips correlated with the spike window on a subset of machines. There was a stray batch job (analytics-job-33) that started around 02:20 on the same cluster, had high CPU+IO and pinned a MIG partition. filing: https://k8s.redwood.internal/pods/analytics-job-33
derek: that could reduce effective SMs and change occupancy heuristics -> cost model prefers smaller kernels that avoid shared mem heavy kernels like flash_attn. So it's a compound issue: driver/triton changes + noisy neighbor reduce headroom.
anya: reproduce plan: 1) force kernel override to flash_attn_fwd for rwbert@v3 shortseq QA on canary hosts; 2) run microbench loops with and without the new driver/triton to compare; 3) instrument cost-model inputs and make decision trace logging more verbose.
sam: please do the override and add an emergency circuit to prefer flash_attn for seq<=32 while we root-cause. We need to avoid regressions on long seqs though.
li: applied override on 3 canaries: `runtimectl set-kernel-policy rwbert@v3 --seq-max 32 --force-kernel flash_attn_fwd --reason "emergency: p99 regression"`
```
deploy-bot: kernel policy applied to 3 nodes: canary-{17,18,19}
```
li: microbench results after override: p99 down to baseline (~1.0x). Profiling now: flash_attn_fwd chosen, exec time ~0.48ms. Looks like override works as mitigation.
anya: good. Next: bisect triton change. li, can you run small repro with triton:2.18.1 vs 2.19.0 and capture kernel-launch params (threads, blocks, shared mem, sm occupancy estimate)? Put results in the thread when ready.
li: started the job. Early diffs: 2.19.0 exposes a different GPU occupancy calc (cuda driver API surface returns different multiprocessor_active_warps) which bumps our estimated_time for flash_attn by ~3x in the cost model for small seqs. Putting more logs now.
sam: if true, propose: a) pin triton to 2.18.x for infra images while we patch cost model; b) add a shortseq override policy until we roll a corrected cost estimator. Which is less disruptive?
derek: pinning triton on infra images is low-risk and isolated. We'll coordinate with infra to roll a targeted rollback for eu-west-1. Also file a patch: change cost estimator to prefer flash_attn when kv_cache_hit_rate >= 0.8 and seq_len<=32; that avoids noisy neighbor false positives.
li: created PR #4876 with updated estimator logic + extra decision trace logging. Tests added (simulation-based).
anya: also add a pipeline that checks kernel selection drift after any driver/triton bump (smoke perf test on shortseq microbench). This should be part of our release checklist.
sam: assign owners: infra rollback: derek; runtime patch + PR: li (review: anya); monitoring + smoke test gating: sam. Aim to rollback tonight and merge runtime patch tomorrow AM.
derek: infra rollback scheduled at 2026-03-17T22:00Z for eu-west-1, will target triton image -> 2.18.1. Notifying oncall.
li: leaving verbose decision traces enabled on canaries for 24h: `/var/log/redwood/runtime/kernel_decisions_verbose.log` - will dump if anything flips back.
sam: thanks all. Keep short updates here. If anyone sees the spike return after rollback, @sam tag me and we'll escalate to immediate revert of driver. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-0317-01 — short-seq p99 regression after triton/driver bump — owner: sam
